findings.defect: Arrival item 40 types fact_ids items as {'type': 'string', 'pattern': '^(<kinds>):'}. The pattern anchors the kind prefix and never requires a local part, so the bare prefix is legal at decode time and unknown at binding time; the whole transaction is spent, which is precisely what the change was written to prevent.
findings.mechanical_proof: Built from the production manifest - reconciliation_schema(load_manifests(Path('prompts'))['source_reconciliation'], units) - the pattern is ^(build_test_asset|dependency|example|format|identity|import_path|inherited_unit|install_command|license|link_target|package|public_symbol|third_party_notices): and re.match accepts every bare prefix that rejected the transaction.
findings.measurement: S4 source_reconciliation rejected twice. Attempt 1: 15 of 40 disposition records carry a bare prefix, 8 distinct kinds (dependency:, example:, identity:, install_command:, license:, link_target:, package:, public_symbol:). Attempt 2: 12 of 40, 7 distinct. The transaction died at S4.
lane_b_additions: The model is filling a slot, not misreading the packet: its own rationale in the same record names the correct ID - example:001, link_target:product.banner, dependency:none, package:cmake_minimum - while fact_ids holds the bare prefix and the rationale says 'used placeholder'.

This is the 'names no fact' branch, not the 32000-token runaway, and it is not confined to a large surface: Email C++'s packet is 357 facts and 225 public symbols, the smallest C++ repository in the lane. Raising or batching the cap alone would leave this draw failing.
fix_options: Strictly correct, and what this same function already does two lines later for unit_id: type fact_ids items as an enum of the packet's fact IDs. binding_errors already refuses anything outside facts.facts, so the enum is exactly co-extensive with what the next stage accepts and admits no bare prefix at all.
Minimal, if an enum of 1651 IDs (PDF C++) is judged too large for the decoder: require a non-empty local part in the pattern.

findings.severity: already in merged history on origin/main; silent; no check looks at it
findings.observed: The shared repository-level .git/config - one file common to the primary checkout and every lane worktree - held user.name=Test / user.email=test@example.com. This branch also acquired 8 fixture commits (5 'seed', 1 'initial', 1 'placeholder') whose whole tree is LICENSE plus README.md, the shape init_git_repository builds. This lane's commit was intact one step down the reflog and was recovered from there; the local override is unset and the commit re-authored.
not_confined_to_this_session: Neither is this lane's, and both landed before this run's first commit.
findings.standing_defect: The git fixtures are unfenced. init_git_repository runs `git config user.email test@example.com` with no --file, no GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and no GIT_DIR, relying entirely on cwd having landed inside a directory git init just created; commit_all relies on cwd alone the same way; run_git adds only GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT/GCM_INTERACTIVE and three -c determinism flags - no GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES, no GIT_DIR, no GIT_CONFIG_* fence. Any such call whose cwd does not land inside a fixture repository operates on the repository git discovers by walking up from the process working directory, which under pytest is the checkout itself.
findings.not_reproduced: A full pytest -n auto run in this worktree immediately after the recovery did NOT reproduce it: 1006 passed, 10 xfailed in 141.50s, with HEAD, the branch ref and git config --local user.name/user.email byte-identical before and after (e2fc2c5 / e2fc2c5 / unset / unset) and a clean git status. The plain suite is therefore not the trigger and this record does not claim it is. The most probable trigger given the timing is two sessions' suites interleaving in one shared git directory - lanes E and F opened at 13:10 (b712790), the same minute the first mis-authored commit landed. Naming the exact race needs an instrumented concurrent run, outside this run's box.
findings.proposal: For whoever owns tests/: fence every fixture call - GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM pointed at a temp file, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES at the fixture root, and git -C <path> with an explicit GIT_DIR - so a fixture can never resolve to the real checkout even when cwd is wrong. Worth doing ahead of the arrival queue: a wrong author is silent and is already in merged history.
findings.alternative_rejected: This lane editing tests/support.py - not an owned path, and a shared-code fix from a lane is what section 28.12 forbids.
